Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `main` at `e7fdd150eb4fe802b6acb711f12f7de7e050e8d3`. The integration-branch mismatch line reads `unknown`, not `true`, so this is not blocked.

## Files likely to change

- `changelog.d/8439-pr-8430-ci-rerun-operator-step.md` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement

None. The change is documentation only.

The fix-up record is one new changelog fragment. It follows the docs-only operator-step pattern in `changelog.d/8330-superseded-host-merge-operator-step.md` and the rule in `changelog.d/8287-operator-step-hold-docs-only-placeholder.md`: a docs-only step names its placeholder only in `changelog.d/`.

Fragment content, kept short and following `docs/changelog-style.md`:

1. First line: `<!-- changelog: changed -->`. This is the same category marker the #8330 precedent uses, and `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` parses it with `CATEGORY_MARKER`.
2. One bullet with a bold headline, for example: **PR #8430's tests-hooks-and-orchestrator CI job waits for an operator to run it again (Refs #8433).**
3. The body says:
   - CI on PR #8430 (head `fd967e4fd1670d91794f890e492ecebcd6702ec3`) failed in the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job.
   - The cause was a transient timeout while cloning the repository at job start. The checkout timed out on all three tries and no test ran.
   - The other four test jobs and `orchestrate-poll` checked out the same commit in the same run and passed, so the code and the workflow file are not at fault.
   - The operator step `CI_RERUN_PR_8430_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` covers running that job again on that head.
   - Nothing reads the placeholder and no code path is gated. Releases, tagging, dispatches, merges, checkout settings and the parity preparation and tests are unchanged.
   - Once the job is rerun, the operator ends the hold on #8433: either post that item's resume command, or set the placeholder as a repository variable. The judge counts a step as done only when such a variable or secret exists or a person resumes the item (#8287 behaviour).
4. The text must not use any auto-close keyword before `#8433` or `#8430`. Use `Refs` only (§21).

## Functions or modules to implement (detail)

None beyond the fragment above. No script, workflow, prompt, test or `agents.d/` fragment is added or edited.

## Data structures affected

None. The new placeholder name `CI_RERUN_PR_8430_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` appears only in the changelog fragment. A check of the working tree found no existing `CI_RERUN` identifier, so the name does not collide with anything.

## API or interface changes

None. The release-time changelog assembly picks the fragment up through its existing path, under the "Changed" category.

## Decisions

### D1 — Record the step only in a changelog.d fragment
- Chosen: one fragment, `changelog.d/8439-pr-8430-ci-rerun-operator-step.md`, that names the placeholder and the operator action.
- Alternatives considered: also adding an `agents.d/` fragment, as #8330 did; adding a `docs/triage/` note like `docs/triage/pr-6611-ci-shard-1.md`; adding an env-var gate in a workflow.
- Why: the issue says the only deliverable is a short note and no workflow, script, test or checkout setting may be edited. The #8287 rule says docs-only steps name their placeholder only in `changelog.d/`. A prior review rejected an unplanned `agents.d/` addition as out of scope (lesson for #8327). A CI rerun is a one-off action, not a lasting contract, so it does not belong in `agents.md`.

### D2 — Fragment category `changed`
- Chosen: `<!-- changelog: changed -->`.
- Alternatives considered: `fixed`.
- Why: nothing is fixed in code. This matches the #8330 operator-step precedent.

## Security considerations

- Trust boundaries touched: none. The change is a markdown fragment that no workflow reads at runtime. The release assembler only concatenates its text.
- Authorization: no new endpoint, worker or surface.
- External input: the fragment holds only fixed facts from the issue (PR number, head SHA, job name). It contains no secrets, tokens, run-log URLs or credentials.
- Abuse cases:
  - An auto-close keyword aimed at #8433 or #8430 would close the blocked item on merge. Mitigation: use `Refs` only, and the PR body must pass `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py`.
  - Gating an existing path behind the placeholder. Mitigation: no code edits at all.

## Potential risks or edge cases

- Conflict note: the issue names the "fix-up record" but no file. This plan reads it as the `changelog.d/` fragment, following #8287 and #8330. Assumption: this issue is #8439, per the memory record "Issue #8439 is clear". If the implementer's issue number differs, the fragment's numeric prefix must use the real one.
- The unblock judge holds #8433 after merge until a person resumes it, the placeholder exists as a repository variable or secret, or `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS` (default 14) runs out. This is intended.
- PR #8430's head `fd967e4f…` cannot be resolved in the sandbox. The plan uses the SHA only as quoted text, so that is harmless.
- A fragment without a valid category marker would be mis-assembled. Mitigation: the first line is exactly `<!-- changelog: changed -->`.

## Testing considerations

- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py tests/test_assemble_changelog.py -q` must stay green.
- `git grep -n CI_RERUN_PR_8430_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` must hit only the new fragment.
- `git diff --stat` must show exactly one added file.
- No new tests: the change is doc-only and existing contract tests cover fragment parsing.

## Pre-execution self-check

- The plan covers the issue's single deliverable: a note with the cause, the head SHA, the job name and the placeholder.
- No existing path is gated, and no workflow, script, test or checkout setting is edited.
- The file list is one exact path with no directory-only tokens.
- §20: no new script or supervisor, so no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry is needed. No scheduler wiring: the operator action is a CI rerun the pipeline must never perform itself.
- §21: `Refs` only, and the PR body is linted.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends changelog.d docs-only operator-step fragment pattern (changelog.d/8330-superseded-host-merge-operator-step.md, assembled by assemble_changelog.py)
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for exactly one note in the fix-up record and forbids changes to workflows, scripts, tests, checkout settings and the parity preparation. The established way to record a docs-only `_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` is a single `changelog.d/` fragment that names the placeholder (#8287, #8330), so the plan keeps exactly that scope. Under the §6 Core Priorities (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), nothing more complete exists here: every extra file would either break the issue's constraints or add an unplanned out-of-scope edit.
